1.title: Services
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Services. It covers the exam area Services and Networking. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Why a Service. Create a Service. Names, D N S and reaching a Service. Troubleshoot a Service. Practice with nine hands-on labs worth forty-six points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Services and Networking (twenty percent). Practice in this module: nine labs, forty-six points, about forty-six minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Why a Service
1.text: Why a Service. The figure shows this: A Service in front of Pods. Exam tip: A Service sends traffic only to Ready Pods whose labels match its selector.

1.title: Why a Service, continued
1.text: Why a Service. Pods come and go, and each new Pod has a new I P address. A Service is a stable virtual I P and D N S name in front of a set of Pods. It picks the Pods with a label selector and spreads connections across the ones that are Ready. The list of Ready Pod addresses is kept in Endpoint Slices ( kube control get endpoints svc still shows the classic view).

1.title: Why a Service, continued
1.text: Why a Service. Cluster I P (default). Reachable from: inside the cluster only. Use it for: internal communication between apps. Node Port. Reachable from: any node I P node Port (thirty thousand to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-seven) and inside. Use it for: simple external access, tests. Load Balancer. Reachable from: an external I P from a cloud load balancer, plus a Node Port and Cluster I P. Use it for: production access on a cloud (here the address stays pending). External Name. Reachable from: inside the cluster; returns a D N S cname. Use it for: a stable in-cluster name for an outside host. headless ( cluster I P None ). Reachable from: D N S returns the Pod I P s directly. Use it for: Stateful Sets, client-side load balancing.

1.title: Create a Service
1.text: Create a Service. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: kube control expose deployment name the port flag the target port flag copies the selector for you.

1.title: Create a Service, continued
1.text: Create a Service. expose copies the selector from the Deployment's Pod labels, so it is the safest way. To fix a node port, generate yamel and add node Port thirty thousand eighty to the port. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create a Service, continued
1.text: Create a Service. port. the port clients use on the Service. target Port. the port on the Pod (default: same as port ); may be the name of a container Port. node Port. the fixed port on every node, Node Port and Load Balancer only. selector. labels of the Pods to serve; a Service without a selector has no automatic endpoints. Several ports: each port needs a unique name. Named target ports ( target Port http ) let the container port number change without touching the Service.

1.title: Names, DNS and reaching a Service
1.text: Names, D N S and reaching a Service. Cluster D N S (Core D N S) gives every Service a name. shop. a Pod in the same namespace. shop dot svc one. any namespace. shop dot svc one dot svc dot cluster dot local. everywhere (the full name). Exam tip: From another namespace, reach a Service as service. namespace.

1.title: Names, DNS and reaching a Service, continued
1.text: Names, D N S and reaching a Service. Test from a throw-away Pod: kube control run temp the rm flag -it the restart flag set to Never the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six then the command W get -q O- -T three H T T P colon slash slash shop dot svc one eighty eighty. Environment variables shop service host and shop service port also appear in Pods created after the Service (the D N S name is the better habit). From your own terminal, reach a Service or Pod without exposing it: k port forward svc slash shop eighty eighty eighty eighty (then curl local host eighty eighty in another terminal), or k port forward pod slash web eighty eighty eighty.

1.title: Troubleshoot a Service
1.text: Troubleshoot a Service. Work from the inside out. These are the classic causes, in the order of how often they appear on the exam. Does the Service have endpoints? Command: kube control get endpoints shop (or kube control get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name shop ). Typical finding: none: the selector matches no Ready Pod. Do the selector and the Pod labels match? Command: kube control get svc shop dash o json path dot spec dot selector and kube control get pods the show labels flag. Typical finding: a typo, or the Service says app web and the Pods say app webapp. Exam tip: Empty endpoints mean the selector matches no Ready Pod; connection refused means a wrong target Port.

1.title: Troubleshoot a Service, continued
1.text: Troubleshoot a Service. Are the Pods Ready? Command: kube control get pods. Typical finding: zero slash one Ready (readiness probe failing) keeps them out of the endpoints. Is target Port the port the app listens on? Command: kube control get svc shop dash o yaml, kube control describe pod. Typical finding: connection refused: wrong target Port. Is the name resolving? Command: kube control exec pod then the command N S lookup shop. Typical finding: wrong namespace in the name. Is a Network Policy blocking? Command: kube control get netpol. Typical finding: Module sixteen. Right namespace? Command: dash n ns. Typical finding: the Service lives in another namespace.

1.title: Troubleshoot a Service, continued
1.text: Troubleshoot a Service. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Troubleshoot a Service, continued
1.text: Troubleshoot a Service. A Service whose selector matches nothing "hangs" (no endpoints, packets go nowhere); a wrong target Port is refused ("connection refused"). Fix the Service, unless the task says to fix the Pods' labels. Exam tip. kube control describe svc name shows the Endpoints line. Empty endpoints mean a selector or readiness problem; filled endpoints but no answer mean a port problem. Exam tip. "Expose the Deployment on port X" is kube control expose deployment name the port flag set to X the target port flag set to container port. Check the Deployment's container port, not just its image.

1.title: Lab 14.1: clusterip service
1.text: Lab fourteen point one: clusterip service. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc one, the Deployment shop (two replicas, engine X alpine, listening on port eighty) exists. Create a Service named shop of type Cluster I P that is reachable inside the cluster on port eighty eighty and forwards to the containers' port eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 14.1: clusterip service, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc one expose deployment shop the port flag set to eighty eighty the target port flag set to eighty. Then kube control dash n svc one get svc shop. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 14.2: nodeport service
1.text: Lab fourteen point two: nodeport service. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc two, expose the Deployment web (engine X on port eighty) with a Service named web np of type Node Port, service port eighty, using the fixed node port thirty thousand eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 14.2: nodeport service, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc two expose deployment web the name flag set to web np the port flag set to eighty the type flag set to Node Port the dry run flag set, and so on. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n svc two apply dash f slash temp slash web np dot yaml. Then kube control dash n svc two get svc web np. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 14.3: fix service selector
1.text: Lab fourteen point three: fix service selector. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc three, the Service api does not work: requests to H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three hang. The Deployment api (two replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three returns the engine X welcome page. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 14.3: fix service selector, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc three get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name api. Then kube control dash n svc three get svc api dash o json path dot spec dot selector echo. Then kube control dash n svc three get pods the show labels flag. Then kube control dash n svc three patch svc api dash p spec selector app api. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 14.4: endpoint ips
2.text: Lab fourteen point four: endpoint ips. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc four, the Service db is backed by several Pods. Write the I P addresses of all Pods that currently serve the Service (one I P per line, sorted) to about slash answers slash endpoints dot txt on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 14.4: endpoint ips, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc four get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name db. Then kube control dash n svc four get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name db dash o json path range dot items dot endpoints dot addresses zero newline end sort about slash, and so on. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 14.5: loadbalancer service
2.text: Lab fourteen point five: loadbalancer service. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc five, expose the Deployment front (engine X, port eighty) with a Service named front lb of type Load Balancer on port eighty. In this test cluster there is no cloud load balancer, so the external address stays pending; only the Service definition is checked. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 14.5: loadbalancer service, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc five expose deployment front the name flag set to front lb the port flag set to eighty the type flag set to Load Balancer. Then kube control dash n svc five get svc front lb. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 14.6: externalname
2.text: Lab fourteen point six: externalname. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc six, create a Service named legacy db that makes the name legacy db dot svc six dot svc dot cluster dot local resolve (as a D N S alias) to the external host db dot example dot com. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 14.6: externalname, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc six create service externalname legacy db the external name flag set to db dot example dot com. Then kube control dash n svc six get svc legacy db. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 14.7: cross namespace dns
2.text: Lab fourteen point seven: cross namespace dns. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The Pod server (engine X) runs in the namespace back and the Pod client (busy box) runs in the namespace front. Make the client able to fetch the engine X page from the server by the name H T T P colon slash slash server dot back (do not touch the Pods). Then write the full D N S name of the Service (including dot svc dot cluster dot local ) to about slash answers slash fqdn dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 14.7: cross namespace dns, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n back expose pod server the port flag set to eighty. Then kube control dash n front exec client then the command W get -q O- -T three H T T P colon slash slash server dot back then pipe to head -three. Then echo server dot back dot svc dot cluster dot local about slash answers slash fqdn dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 14.8: multiport service
2.text: Lab fourteen point eight: multiport service. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc eight, the Deployment app (two replicas) has Pods that listen on port eighty (web) and eighty eighty (metrics; the image is engine X so only eighty answers, the definition is what counts). Create a Service named app that exposes two named ports: http on port eighty targeting container port eighty, and metrics on port nine thousand ninety targeting container port eighty eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 14.8: multiport service, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n svc eight apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n svc eight get svc app. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 14.9: fix target port
2.text: Lab fourteen point nine: fix target port. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc nine, requests to H T T P colon slash slash site dot svc nine fail with "connection refused". The Deployment site (two replicas of engine X alpine, which listens on port eighty) is healthy and the Service site selects its Pods correctly. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that H T T P colon slash slash site dot svc nine returns the engine X welcome page. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 14.9: fix target port, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc nine get endpoints site. Then kube control dash n svc nine get svc site dash o json path dot spec dot ports zero echo. Then kube control dash n svc nine patch service site the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash ports slash zero slash target Port, value eighty. Then probe H T T P colon slash slash site dot svc nine svc nine then pipe to head -three. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What decides which Pods a Service sends traffic to? Answer: Its label selector, and only Pods that are Ready. Question two. What is the difference between port, target Port and node Port? Answer: port is the Service's port, target Port is the Pod's port, node Port is the fixed port on every node (Node Port and Load Balancer). Question three. What range do node ports use? Answer: thirty thousand to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-seven by default.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the full D N S name of Service shop in namespace svc one? Answer: shop dot svc one dot svc dot cluster dot local. Question five. What does empty endpoints for a Service mean? Answer: No Ready Pod matches the selector: check labels and readiness. Question six. What does an External Name Service return? Answer: A D N S cname (canonical name record) to the external host name; it has no selector and no proxying.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. How do you reach a Service from your terminal without exposing it? Answer: kube control port forward svc or name local port. Question eight. What is a headless Service? Answer: A Service with cluster I P None: D N S returns the Pod I P s, not one virtual I P.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Types: Cluster I P, Node Port (thirty thousand to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-seven), Load Balancer, External Name, headless. Create: kube control expose deployment x the port flag the target port flag the type flag. Ports: port (Service), target Port (Pod, number or name), node Port. D N S: svc, svc dot ns, svc dot ns dot svc dot cluster dot local. Endpoints: selector must match Ready Pods; get endpoints, describe svc. Debug: selector versus labels, readiness, target Port, namespace, Network Policy. Local test: port forward, a throw-away busy box Pod with W get.
